properties.decision:
**DECIDED 2026-08-19 BY ANTHONY — option (f), on his instruction "yes, build it as you recommend".** Delivered the same day, `epoch:the-loop-holds-the-invitation`; what is owed is stated in `req:detecting-is-not-asking`.

**THE RULING: REPORTING A GAP AND INVITING ITS CLOSURE ARE DIFFERENT ACTS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS URGENT.** Detection stays unconditional and cheap. The *invitation* waits for a boundary — the user asks, pauses, says they are done, or turns to building. **The gaps stay LOUD throughout: this defers the invitation, never the record.**

He chose it over a user-set posture, a computed phase, and full lifecycle phases — all of which ask the user to declare something, when the measured complaint was simply being interrupted.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐⭐ ALEX'S ANSWER IS WHY THIS WAS ANSWERABLE, AND IT KILLED THE FAVOURITE HYPOTHESIS

Asked what was actually pushing him to close: *"I would enter some information about the application. Like this data model does this and this does this and then it basically would respond with, **'I have those all recorded. There are open gaps with X, Y, and Z. Do you want to fix them?'**"*

**IT WAS NOT VOLUME.** Three gaps — "X, Y, and Z" — not three hundred. The leading hypothesis was the chatty `unsatisfied_requirement` detector burying a corpus, and **that fix would not have touched his problem.** `dec:gap-reporting-when-most-intent-is-unbuilt` is a real defect and a genuinely different one; the two only looked alike.

**AND HE REQUESTED NONE OF IT.** No `loop_status`, no `detect_gaps`, no status readout. Every prompt was volunteered and ended in a question he had to answer in order to keep doing what he came to do.

**HIS ASK WAS A DEFERRAL, NOT A SILENCING:** *"let me finish inputting the knowledge into this, **then we can discuss how to close gaps and issues**."*

📌 THE QUESTION WAS PUT TO HIM PRECISELY BECAUSE THE ANSWER WOULD PICK THE OPTION, and it did. Recorded because it is the cheapest move in this whole node: one question to the affected user eliminated one option outright, demoted two others, and produced a fix nobody had proposed.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 IT WAS NOT A BUG — THREE SERVED SOURCES INSTRUCTED IT, EACH CORRECT ALONE

  1. `capture-intent` step 7 — *"when it names debt, run detect-and-ask before the next operational task, not after."*
  2. served `AGENTS.md` step 2 — *"DETECT gaps and ask… ask the user… Do this before building."*
  3. `detect-and-ask`'s own trigger — *"after capturing new intent."*

**Each was written for a real failure** — the agent that only ever adds nodes and surfaces nothing, which `capture-intent` step 7 names in as many words. **Together, on a user doing nothing but capture for days, they produce a prompt to close after every message.** That is why the fix is a timing rule added to all three rather than the deletion of any one, and why none of them was wrong to exist.

⭐⭐ **CORROBORATED FROM THE INSIDE, SAME WEEK.** During the session that recorded this node, the Stop hook fired at the agent — *"6 graph write(s) this session and no loop check… intent was captured this session and detect_gaps was never run"* — **in the middle of a BRAINSTORM**, the one workflow whose own skill says *"do not run detect-and-ask over brainstormed nodes… it would ask the user to firm up exactly what they deliberately left soft."* The loop pushed toward closure at the moment its own doctrine forbids it. Alex's report and that observation are the same defect at two distances, and the ruling covers both.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
ANTHONY'S ORIGINAL FRAMING, AND WHY IT IS NOT WHAT SHIPPED

His proposal was user-defined phases — *"design conception, initial systems engineering, design implementation, testing, fielding."* ⚠️ **He qualified it in the same breath:** *"projects like reflow2 often will be continually developed and I will probably always have ideas, so the phases would probably need to be more advisory and fluid than hard phases."* The evidence backs the caveat: `fact:the-owner-uses-reflow2-as-a-funnel-for-random-order-input` measured nine inputs in one day arriving in random order, with *"both my brother and I kind of work like this."* **No ordered phase list predicts that — and in the end no phase concept was needed at all**, because the complaint was about interruption, not about stage.

📌 `maturity_report` already sees where a design sits and deliberately refuses to say where it SHOULD be. 📌 `set_project_mode` gates only `apply_heal`; it was never this. 📌 `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` (**`proposed`, still unaccepted**) already states Alex's mode — *"every capability is `planned`, every requirement `proposed`… which is honest and must not read as catastrophic."*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
OPTIONS AS THEY STOOD

(f) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — separate reporting from prompting in the served text. Changes no computation, no schema, no detector; keeps every gap loud; fixes the brainstorm collision too.
(a) **NOT CHOSEN** — a stated, user-set posture. Heavier than the evidence demanded: Alex never asked for a mode, he asked not to be interrupted. A stale posture would also silence the loop exactly when it matters.
(b) **NOT CHOSEN** — derive from `maturity_report`'s frontier. Would make what the loop asks depend on a computed phase, converting a reading into a judgement.
(c) 🛑 **ELIMINATED BY THE ANSWER** — aggregate the chatty detector. Three gaps, not three hundred. Still a live defect elsewhere.
(d) **NOT CHOSEN** — a session capture mode. reflow2 has no clock and no session identity; "for this session" is the harness's concept.
(e) **NOT CHOSEN** — full lifecycle phases; retracted by their own author.

⚠️ **THE HONEST WEAKNESS OF WHAT SHIPPED**, stated rather than discovered later: served prose with nothing able to observe whether it holds. `skill_lint` asserts the text is present and mirrored; it cannot assert an agent honoured it. **Same shape as the instruction that lapsed within four days in `dec:idea-the-enum-question-came-back-four-days-after-it-was-fixed`.**

⚠️ AND ONE JUDGEMENT STAYS THE AGENT'S: *"plainly still pouring things in"* is not computable from the graph — the signals are conversational and live where reflow2 cannot see them. The explicit boundaries are named in the served text so the rule can never be read as "never ask".
properties.name: DECIDED — detecting is not asking: the loop keeps finding gaps and holds the invitation to close until the person stops pouring things in
properties.rationale: Raised 2026-08-18 from Alex's report, answered by him 2026-08-19, and settled the same day on Anthony's instruction to build the recommendation. The answer is preserved verbatim because it eliminated the volume hypothesis — which was the favourite and would have sent the fix at a different defect entirely — and because the whole episode is the cheapest thing in the node: one question to the affected user killed one option, demoted two, and produced a fix nobody had proposed. The three served sources are named with file and step so a future session does not simply delete one; each was written for a real failure and only their combination was the defect. The Stop-hook self-observation is kept because self-measurement of the defect under discussion, during a brainstorm the skill explicitly protects, is stronger than a relayed report alone. Anthony's own phase proposal and his same-breath retraction are both retained so the record shows the idea was taken seriously and then rendered unnecessary rather than rejected.
